hypothesis: A larger increase in reported jet-fuel spot prices is associated with lower subsequent airline total return minus SPY total return.
exposure: Continuous percent change over five reported EIA observations; elapsed calendar days retained; no optimized threshold.
entry_rule: First verified exchange-session close strictly after independently established signal availability. Observation dates alone never establish availability.
exit_rule: Close exactly 5 or 10 verified exchange sessions after entry; missing entry, exit, or adjustment evidence excludes the outcome.
price_basis: Same-vendor documented dividend-and-split-adjusted close series for airline and benchmark. Subtract benchmark total return over identical endpoints; no raw/adjusted mixing.
controls_draft: Calendar effects fixed before outcome inspection
dependence: Shared fuel shocks across companies and overlapping forward windows require dependence-aware uncertainty; company rows are not independent trials.
evaluation: Predeclare chronological training/validation/locked holdout dates and minimum sample before reading new outcomes. Compare controls-only versus controls-plus-fuel. Report all horizons, uncertainty, exclusions and incremental out-of-sample performance. Register executable prices, costs and a separate strategy before claiming tradability.
lock_blockers: Licensed daily adjusted price source and adjustment policy
Availability evidence source and conservative decision schedule
Fixed sample dates, minimum sample and uncertainty method
quarterly_role: Business context only; quarterly margin associations are not evidence of days-to-weeks stock-return predictability.
